Avery / Soojin —

I pulled together the technical narrative draft below and started the matrix CSV (see attachments list). Key points to include:

- Topology overview (1 para): Redwood supports three runtime modalities: Hosted (public API), Dedicated (customer-reserved GPU pools with isolated tenant routing), and Private (customer-managed VPCs with a customer-controlled control plane option). For Private, our optional private control plane terminates management traffic inside the customer VPC/partner-managed subnet, while our provisioning/observability telemetry can be routed to customer endpoints or retained in Redwood with access controls.

- Control plane vs data plane (1 para): The control plane handles orchestration (model versioning, rollouts, health checks) and uses mutual TLS and identity-based certificates. Data plane (inference traffic) is pinned to tenant-specific GPU pools for Dedicated and to customer VPC routing for Private. KV caches and session keys are logically partitioned per-tenant; customer-managed KMS (via KMS/HSM integration) can be used for key wrapping.

- Isolation controls (bulleted):
  * Network ACLs and microsegmentation per compute pool
  * Per-tenant routing tables and subnet allocation for Dedicated GPU pools
  * Optional air-gapped deployment for high-regulated customers (Private airgap image + offline onboarding)
  * KV/HSM boundary: keys never transit public endpoints; key material is wrapped by customer KMS where required
  * Fallback model policy: policy-based routing that prefers Dedicated variant, falls back to cost-compatible hosted variant in cross-region capacity events

- Audit and evidence (1 para): Logging (TLS session metadata, request IDs, model version) is available per tenant; for SOC 2 we provide redacted audit samples and a map of retention policies. Pen-test results and monthly integrity checks are summarized in the SOC 2 packet.

I will attach the in-progress isolation matrix and a pointer to the diagram in Drive; Soojin, can you produce the one-pager topology PDF (redacted) and add a simple legend that shows which components are shared vs dedicated?

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Date: 2025-05-16T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on KV/HSM boundary

David / Sarah / Avery —

Short answer for auditors: when customer-managed KMS/HSM is configured for Private deployments, key material is never unwrapped in Redwood-managed memory. We support envelope encryption where customer root keys are held in the customer KMS/HSM and only wrapped keys transit to Redwood; unwrapping occurs in the customer boundary or in a dedicated, customer-provisioned HSM when explicitly contracted. For Dedicated deployments using Redwood-managed HSM, there is explicit tenancy isolation and keys used for runtime wrapping are stored in tenant-scoped HSM partitions; we can provide an architecture snapshot of that flow in the SIG appendix.

I will update the SIG answers appendix and attach the finalized CSV mapping to evidence items. Packaging next: Avery, if you can confirm the redaction (remove customer IPs and any tenant IDs), I’ll hand off the package.

-Kimberly
